hdp-chronic.setting: Usually outpatient; admit for severe BP or complications
outpatient: Stable treated chronic hypertension can be followed in clinic with a recorded maternal/fetal surveillance plan.
admit: Severe-range BP (systolic ≥160 or diastolic ≥110 mmHg), symptoms suggesting superimposed pre-eclampsia, concerning blood tests or fetal compromise need hospital assessment; admit when surveillance/treatment cannot be delivered safely outside hospital.
ready: Severe BP has resolved on an established oral plan; symptoms, renal/liver/platelet results and fetal assessment have been reviewed.
After birth, BP and medicine review must be arranged before leaving; a single normal reading is insufficient after recent severe hypertension.
medicines: Continue the selected maintenance medicine with a written dose and adjustment plan. Stop methyldopa within 2 days after birth and substitute if needed; do not automatically stop every antihypertensive.
Check breastfeeding compatibility and renal function/potassium for postpartum enalapril; it is not an antenatal medicine.
tests: Document baseline/recent creatinine, urine protein and other tests indicated by the presentation; schedule follow-up for any abnormality.
homeCare: Give a written BP-monitoring schedule, thresholds for contacting the unit and named responsibility for prescription changes.

followUp.when: After birth: first 2 days and day 3–5
followUp.action: Arrange BP measurement; continue the individual monitoring schedule if abnormal.
Review antihypertensive treatment at 2 weeks; review longer-term BP and cardiovascular/renal care at 6–8 weeks.

returnImmediately: Severe headache, visual change, epigastric/right-upper-quadrant pain, chest pain, breathlessness or a severe BP reading require urgent reassessment.

medicineDetails.when: A selected maintenance option when prescribed.
An alternative maintenance option; use the modified-release formulation specified.

hdp-gestational.setting: Outpatient surveillance if stable; admit severe hypertension
outpatient: Non-severe gestational hypertension does not require automatic admission when investigations, fetal wellbeing and reliable follow-up are reassuring.
admit: Admit severe hypertension; assess for pre-eclampsia when symptoms, proteinuria, laboratory abnormalities or fetal concerns develop.
ready: No severe BP or evolving pre-eclampsia; a stable oral regimen and a feasible maternal/fetal follow-up plan are documented.
After birth, complete symptom/BP assessment and communicate the plan for the expected postpartum BP rise.
medicines: Continue indicated antihypertensive treatment; stop methyldopa within 2 days of birth. Record the prescriber and thresholds for reducing/stopping treatment rather than advising the patient to stop on their own.
tests: Record the urine protein and blood-test assessment used to exclude pre-eclampsia; repeat sooner if the clinical state changes.
homeCare: Teach correct BP measurement if home monitoring is used and provide an urgent-contact number.

followUp.when: After birth: first 2 days and day 3–5
followUp.action: Check BP; prescribe additional checks for abnormal readings.

followUp.when: 2 weeks if on medication; 6–8 weeks for all
followUp.action: Review treatment and whether hypertension has resolved; persistent hypertension needs ongoing primary/specialist care.

returnImmediately: Headache, visual symptoms, upper abdominal pain, breathlessness, seizures or severe BP need immediate assessment, including after delivery.

medicineDetails.when: Use only if this is the selected discharge antihypertensive.
Alternative maintenance option; do not substitute the acute immediate-release sequence.

hdp-pre-eclampsia.setting: Hospital assessment; severe disease needs admission and possible critical care
outpatient: Antenatal outpatient care is a specialist decision only when maternal/fetal assessment and reliable surveillance support it; recent eclampsia or HELLP is not a routine outpatient pathway.
admit: Admit for severe/persistent hypertension, seizure or neurological symptoms, pulmonary oedema, renal/liver/platelet deterioration, significant pain or fetal compromise.
Eclampsia/HELLP or organ-support needs require appropriate high-dependency/critical-care monitoring, with transfer after initial stabilisation when necessary.
ready: Postnatal NICE transfer criteria: no pre-eclampsia symptoms, BP ≤150/100 mmHg with or without treatment, and blood results stable or improving; all criteria must be met.

Following eclampsia/HELLP, complete indicated seizure prophylaxis/monitoring and document neurological, respiratory, urine-output and blood-test recovery before considering home care. Critical-care step-down and discharge home are separate decisions.
medicines: Continue the selected oral antihypertensive. Stop methyldopa within 2 days after birth; document replacement and review.

The prescriber should consider reduction below 140/90 and reduce below 130/80 mmHg under NICE; provide an individual written adjustment plan. Magnesium loading/infusions are inpatient treatment, not take-home medication.
tests: Review platelet count, transaminases and creatinine at 48–72 hours after birth/critical-care step-down; abnormal results need a repeat plan until recovery.
At 6–8 weeks check urine protein; persistent proteinuria (1+ or more) needs a 3-month renal review and referral if kidney function is abnormal.
homeCare: Provide the BP schedule, named reviewer, medicine list and explicit severe-symptom instructions. Discuss recurrence, future-pregnancy planning and long-term cardiovascular risk.

followUp.action: NICE BP surveillance until off treatment with no hypertension; adapt intensity to findings.

followUp.when: If not on antihypertensives: day 3–5 after birth
followUp.action: Check BP; repeat on alternate days if abnormal.

followUp.when: 2 weeks if still on treatment; 6–8 weeks for all
followUp.action: Review medicines, BP, recovery and urine protein; arrange renal follow-up when indicated.

returnImmediately: Seizure, severe/persistent headache, visual disturbance, epigastric pain, dyspnoea, chest pain or severe BP: return immediately; postpartum onset can occur after discharge.

medicineDetails.when: One selected oral BP option; do not prescribe every alternative together.
Alternative/adjunct only within the documented BP plan.
Postpartum only when prescribed, with renal function/potassium monitoring.
